cohort: The study included 159 primigravidas with a singleton, uncomplicated pregnancy.
finding: Uterocervical angle (UCA) was found to be a better predictor of spontaneous preterm birth compared to cervical length (CL), with a strong correlation between an obtuse UCA and an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth.
cross-section timing: Measurements for UCA and CL were taken at 16 to 24 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: Measurements were performed at 16 to 24 weeks of gestation; outcomes were categorized by gestational age at delivery (<34 weeks, 34-37 weeks, <37 weeks).
